To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the inactivation of calcium currents in mammalian pitutary tumor cells ( GH3 ) is dependent upon intracellular calcium accumulation, that the inactivation is reduced or eliminated by increasing the concentration of cyclic AMP within the cell, that the calcium channels inactivate more rapidly at more positive potentials, and that the inactivation process can be described quantitatively by an equation that includes the concentration of free calcium in the cell.

the inactivation of calcium currents in mammalian cells is dependent on calcium entry through the same channels that carry the current, that inactivation of these channels is voltage dependent, and that inactivation of the calcium current can be reduced by intracellular cAMP.
inactivation of the calcium channels in GH 3 cells is dependent on calcium entry and intracellular calcium accumulation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanism of inactivation of calcium currents in pituitary tumor GH3 cells.
the regulation of the calcium current through the dihydropiridine sensitive calcium channels in the pituitary tumor cell, GH3.
the molecular mechanism of the inactivation of dihydropyri dine-sensitive calcium channels in mammal pituitary tumor cell (GH3).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the inactivation of the calcium channels of GH3 cells is a calcium- dependent process that is modulated by cAMP.

the calcium current through the dihydropyrine-sensitive calcium channels is inactivated by calcium entry and that the inactivation can be prevented by intracellular calcium buffering, by extracellular calcium replacement, by depolarization to more positive potentials, or by activation of cAMP-dependent protein kinase.
calcium-dependent inactivation of dihydropyriidine-sensitive calcium channels in pituitary cells is a consequence of intracellular calcium accumulation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
calcium entry through the channels activates a mechanism for their own inactivation.

calcium channels in GH 3 cells inactivate when they are opened by a voltage step and that this inactivation can be prevented by either reducing the calcium influx during the step or by increasing the intracellular calcium buffering.
the dihydropiridine-sensitive calcium channels in mammallian pituitary tumor cell (GH3) inactivate when membrane depolarisation leads to calcium ion entrance and intracellular accumulation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the calcium-dependent inactivation of calcium currents is not a general property of all calcium channels, but is restricted to channels that are modulated by dihydropridines and cAMP.
inactivation of the channels is not due to a direct interaction of calcium with the channel protein but is instead mediated by the rise in intracellular free calcium.
the inactivation of calcium currents is not a general property of calcium channels.
